docs.title: ‘Centre weighing Rs 35,000-cr outlay for PM-KUSUM-II’: MNRE’s Santosh Kumar Sarangi
docs.text: The government is considering an outlay of around Rs 35,000 crore for a follow-up to PM-KUSUM, broadly in line with the existing scheme, while seeking to link farm solarisation more closely with efficient irrigation and water conservation, MNRE Secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi told FE. He also explained how the government seeks to resolve a tapering demand for "vanilla" solar projects, and why "acceptable prices" are important to attract buyers. Edited excerpts: Q. What is being planned after PM-KUSUM? Could the new programme have an outlay similar to the existing scheme? ALSO READRs 1.86 lakh cr grid push: 2 ‘under-the-radar’ transformer stocks with 40%+ ROCE A. The financial support could be broadly similar to the existing PM-KUSUM outlay, though the final amount has not been decided. The next phase is being discussed with the Agriculture Ministry with a greater focus on convergence between renewable energy and agriculture. It could incorporate modern water-conservation measures and more effective irrigation planning, rather than treating solar pumps as a standalone intervention. The structure and funding mechanism are still under discussion. The existing PM-KUSUM programme has central financial support of about Rs 34,422 crore. In several cases work is going on in the current scheme but payments have not been made. So there may be some spillover (in case of funds). In the case of legacy schemes, any legacy amount usually gets carried forward. Q. A large renewable project pipeline is facing delays in signing PPAs and PSAs. A. Some developers might exit as demand for plain, or “vanilla”, solar projects (those without backward integration/storage support etc.) has weakened. Recent regulatory changes have provided an exit route without the earlier consequence of forfeiting certain bank guarantees linked to connectivity. Some people will exit because the interest in vanilla solar is not very high. But vanilla solar with BESS is now selling well. Rather than simply replacing every surrendered project with an identical tender, SECI is being asked to first understand what states and distribution companies actually require. What we have now pushed SECI to do is to constantly talk to the states and discoms, understand their power profile and requirements, and only after understanding bring out those bids. The idea was you keep on tendering, people will eventually buy. But we have reached a point where people are not going to buy vanilla solar. You have to offer them in a configuration that will be acceptable to them, and not only configuration but also the prices that are acceptable. Q. Can India sustain renewable additions of around 50 GW annually? A. This will be sustainable provided we also pick up on battery manufacturing capacity. Dependence on imported batteries currently creates long delivery periods. Domestic manufacturing could accelerate storage deployment substantially. CEA projections envisage another 400 GW of renewable capacity by 2035–36, requiring battery storage, pumped hydro and green hydrogen to support growing solar and wind generation. Q. Where does PM Surya Ghar stand against its one-crore household target? A. Around 60 lakh households have been covered so far, with installations expected to cross 85 lakh and potentially reach 90 lakh by March 2027. ALSO READ2 Electrolyser stocks in India’s Rs 19,744-cr green hydrogen race—Who has the edge? It has picked up pace, so we are confident of touching 85 to 90 [lakh]. The remaining roughly 10 lakh could take “one or two months” beyond March. Q. Why has offshore wind failed to attract the same investor interest as solar and onshore wind? A. Economics remain difficult. Onshore wind costs about Rs 7-7.5 crore/MW, against roughly Rs 25 crore/MW for offshore wind. Offshore power could cost around Rs 8-9/unit, while solar is available at Rs 2.40-2.50. In India's case, the choice today is not compelling in favour of offshore wind because you have alternative access to cheaper electricity. The ministry is examining ways to attract developers without committing substantially higher incentives.

docs.title: How to Build a More Resilient Fixed Income Portfolio
docs.text: Recent policy actions from major central banks have again brought interest rates into focus. Whether it is the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) maintaining a firm stance on inflation risks or the US Federal Reserve (Fed) signaling that policy may need to remain restrictive for longer, bond markets globally continue to adjust to a higher-for-longer interest rate environment. For fixed income investors, periods such as these often warrant a review of portfolio exposures. Not necessarily because an immediate change is required, but because the backdrop that worked in one rate cycle may not hold in another. The challenge today is not merely the level of rates. Rather, it is the degree of uncertainty surrounding their future trajectory. ALSO READBond yields at a 3-year high: Should you stop equity SIPs and invest in debt funds? Bond Markets and the Repricing of Expectations Bond yields are driven not only by current policy rates but also by expectations regarding future inflation trajectory, growth and central bank actions regarding policy rates. As these expectations evolve, bond markets periodically reprice. In such environments, volatility in fixed income markets may appear counterintuitive. Bonds are generally perceived to be associated with lower volatility, yet periods of policy uncertainty can lead to meaningful fluctuations in prices, particularly in longer-duration segments of the market. This dynamic has been visible across global bond markets in recent years. Episodes where investors anticipated imminent rate cuts have often been followed by renewed concerns around inflation persistence or fiscal pressures, resulting in repeated adjustments in yield expectations. The Question Is Not Whether Rates Rise or Fall One of the commonly occurring considerations in fixed income investing is to anchor portfolios around a single interest-rate outcome. But markets generally don’t tend to move in a straight line. Even during broader easing cycles, yields can periodically rise. Similarly, during tightening phases, sections of the yield curve may behave differently than expected. As a result, portfolio construction may warrant greater attention than rate forecasting itself. The focus, in many cases, shifts from attempting to anticipate the next policy move towards assessing whether the risks embedded within a portfolio remain commensurate with the investor's objectives and investment horizon. Duration Risk Deserves Closer Attention In periods where rate expectations remain fluid, duration becomes increasingly relevant. Longer-duration portfolios tend to exhibit more sensitivity to changes in bond yields. While such exposure may benefit portfolios if yields decline materially, the same characteristic could contribute to elevated mark-to-market volatility if rates remain elevated or rise further. ALSO READBond yields are rising and debt fund NAVs under pressure: Should you stay invested or exit? This does not imply that longer-duration strategies are inappropriate. Rather, it highlights the importance of understanding the role they play within an overall portfolio. For investors with shorter investment horizons or lower tolerance for interim volatility, strategies positioned at the shorter end of the maturity spectrum may offer a different risk-return profile compared with longer-duration alternatives. Yield Alone May Not Provide the Complete Picture Periods of elevated interest rates often bring another visible feature: higher advertised yields. While attractive yields naturally draw investor attention, the source of those yields warrants equal scrutiny. In fixed income, incremental yield may arise from several factors, including: Longer maturity exposure; Lower credit quality; Reduced liquidity; or Structural portfolio positioning. Viewed in isolation, a higher portfolio yield may provide only a partial picture. A useful question for investors may not be - whether a particular portfolio offers a higher yield, but rather what risks are being undertaken to generate that additional yield. Credit Quality Remains a Key Consideration Interest-rate risk tends to be immediately visible through changes in market prices. Credit risk, by contrast, often emerges gradually. As a result, periods of market adjustment can reinforce the importance of understanding the quality profile of underlying holdings. Investors evaluating debt strategies may wish to consider whether additional return expectations are being derived from duration positioning, credit exposure, or a combination of both. Where interest-rate volatility is already a feature of the environment, some investors may prefer to understand whether additional layers of risk are also being introduced. The objective is not to avoid risk altogether but to ensure that risks are deliberate, understood and aligned with the intended role of the allocation. Carry and Roll-Down: Returning to Fixed Income Fundamentals In recent years, discussions around fixed income have frequently centered on duration calls and policy expectations. However, in a higher-yield environment, traditional sources of bond returns such as carry and roll-down may regain prominence. Carry represents the income generated from holding a bond portfolio over time, while roll-down reflects the impact of bonds moving closer to maturity along the yield curve. When yields are elevated relative to recent history, these return drivers may contribute meaningfully to overall outcomes, even in the absence of capital appreciation. For this reason, strategies that seek to capture carry while maintaining disciplined risk management continue to attract investor attention across market cycles. docs.title: Deep market liquidity enables easy exits: FM
docs.text:
Sign In 
 CLOSE 
 For uninterrupted reading, switch to App
 READ IN APP 
 Written by FE Bureau 
 October 19, 2026 20:56 IST 
 Follow Us 
 Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has rejected the view that persistent weakness in the Indian rupee is driving portfolio outflows, maintaining that India’s economic fundamentals remain strong. She, however, added that India’s capital markets are among the world’s most liquid, allowing global investors to enter and exit positions with relative ease
“I would say the fundamentals of the Indian economy are fine,” Sitharaman told CNBC on the sidelines of the IMF – World Bank meetings in Bangkok on Friday when asked whether portfolio outflows were due to the persistent weakness in the rupee.
“India is probably the second-largest liquid market available, and because of the ease of liquidity and availability, investors can also exit easily. There is no fundamental weakness,” she asserted.
Strong domestic inflows, particularly through mutual funds, have helped absorb heavy foreign selling and cushion market volatility. The T+1 settlement cycle also enables faster trade settlement, while a busy IPO market offers investors additional exit opportunities. Together, these factors have helped India’s markets withstand $33 billion in foreign outflows in 2026 without triggering broader economic instability.
The rupee hit a record low of 96.96 per US dollar in May 2026 due to surging oil prices and heavy capital outflows amid the West Asia conflict. After hovering near those lows in early October 2026, the currency corrected sharply by nearly 2% to close at 94.92 on October 16 following aggressive dollar-supply measures and derivative curbs introduced by the Reserve Bank of India on October 12.
“The risks that we are facing now, even in 2027, I guess those are risks that we will have to face,” she said, referring to the three ‘Fs’ –fuel, fertiliser and foreign exchange.
Elaborating on the challenges, Sitharaman said crude oil prices , rather than the availability of supplies, remained a key concern for India. While supplies were available, the cost of imports could pressure the economy, particularly if global oil prices remain elevated.
Fertiliser prices and availability were another concern, she said, pointing to a shrinking pool of suppliers as some countries prioritise domestic requirements over exports. Securing supplies on time and at affordable prices would remain a challenge.
Sitharaman also flagged the movement of global capital towards artificial intelligence and the United States as a concern for investment in other economies. Capital that would typically flow across countries and sectors, including renewable energy and advanced chemistry, could become harder to access as investors concentrate on these opportunities.
She said fuel, foreign exchange and capital flows would remain key challenges for India in 2027, with foreign direct investment also warranting attention.
On whether India could absorb another energy supply shock given the state of public finances, Sitharaman said the government had maintained sufficient buffers to manage disruptions in crude oil supplies. These cushions had not been used significantly during the year, although some support was required during difficulties involving cooking gas.
She added that a constraint on availability would pose a greater risk than price increases alone, but said India had identified alternative sources of supply.
Asked how sustained or higher Brent crude prices would affect public finances, Sitharaman said, “It will be a challenge. To what extent, I can’t speculate,” she added.

docs.title: Dividend, stock split, buyback: Last chance to buy today - VRL Logistics, JSW Dulux, Angel One shares
docs.text:
Dividend, stock split, buyback: Last chance to buy today - VRL Logistics, JSW Dulux, Angel One shares
 TIPSMUSIC 
 New Delhi, Oct. 20 -- VRL Logistics, JSW Dulux, Tips Music and Angel One are likely to attract investors' attention on Wednesday, October 21, as shareholders track upcoming dividend payouts, a stock split, a share buyback and key record dates. 
 VRL Logistics has revised the record date for its share buyback, while JSW Dulux has fixed October 22 as the record date for its proposed 1:10 stock split. 
 Meanwhile, Tips Music and Angel One have fixed October 22 as the record date for their respective corporate actions. Tips Music has announced an interim dividend of Rs.6.50 per share, while Angel One has declared a second interim dividend of Rs.1.40 per equity share for FY27. 
 Investors looking to benefit from this payout must ensure they own the stock before the record date. Under India's T+1 settlement cycle, shares purchased on or after the record date will not qualify for the dividend. 
 VRL Logistics has revised the record date for its share buyback to October 22, 2026, from the earlier date of October 16, 2026. The company announced the change in a regulatory filing, stating that a corrigendum to the public announcement, originally published on October 8, 2026, had been issued to reflect the revised date. 
 The record date will determine which shareholders are eligible to participate in the buyback. Earlier this month, the company approved a buyback of 87.5 lakh fully paid-up equity shares, representing 5% of its paid-up equity share capital, at Rs.320 per share. 
 The buyback will be carried out through the tender offer route on a proportionate basis, with the total buyback size capped at Rs.280 crore. 
 Paints and coatings maker JSW Dulux, formerly known as Akzo Nobel India, has fixed October 22, 2026, as the record date for its proposed 1:10 stock split. Under the plan, each fully paid-up equity share with a face value of Rs.10 will be subdivided into 10 equity shares with a face value of Re 1 each. 
 The stock split follows JSW Paints' acquisition of a 60.76% stake in Akzo Nobel India in December 2025. 
 Tips Music has announced an interim dividend of Rs.6.50 per share and fixed October 22 as the record date. 
 In its earnings filing on October 15, the company said, "During the quarter, the Company successfully completed a share buyback of Rs.44.44 crore and has also announced interim dividend of Rs.6.50 per share reflecting our continued focus on delivering value to shareholders." 
 Angel One has fixed October 22, 2026, as the record date to determine shareholder eligibility for its second interim dividend of Rs.1.40 per equity share of Re 1 face value for the financial year 2026-27. 
 The dividend will be paid on or before November 14, 2026, to eligible shareholders whose names appear in the company's register of members or depository records as of the record date.

docs.title: Buy Sobha Ltd for the Target Rs.1,710 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Multiple new launches expected in 2H Strong operational performance; Bangalore remains top performer 
Sobha reported 16% YoY pre-sales growth to INR22.1b in 2QFY27 (second highest-ever bookings after 1QFY27), driven by mix of sustenance sales and new launches. It launched two projects in 2Q – Sobha Boulevard in Mysuru (plotted development) with GDV of INR1.2b and Sobha Bellevue in Calicut with GDV of INR11.5b. In 2QFY27, Bangalore remained the largest contributor with 60% share of the quarter’s presales, followed by NCR at 27% and Kerala at 10%. In terms of price segments, INR20-30m/unit contributed ~30% to the presales, followed by 26% from >INR50m. In 1HFY27, the company clocked INR59b in presales, of which 70% came from new launches.
 Strong launch pipeline; well on track for 30% YoY growth 
The company’s forthcoming launch pipeline consists of 18 projects covering 20.4msf (INR314b GDV), out of which 12msf (GDV of ~INR180b) across eight projects is expected to be launched during 2HFY27. This pipeline comprises three projects in Bengaluru and one project each in Hyderabad, Chennai, Gurgaon, Greater Noida and Thrissur. It also has ~INR229b worth inventory across its ongoing projects. Sobha has maintained 30% YoY presales growth guidance for FY27, which translates into ~INR105b in presales. We bake in a 27% CAGR in presales to INR130b during FY26-28E.
 Highest quarterly collections; land payments increase 
In 2QFY27, collections from the residential segment grew 4% YoY to INR19.2b, recording the highest-ever quarterly collections, driven by the deferred collections from 1QFY27. Net operational cash flow (NOCF) declined 14% YoY to INR4.4b, with NOCF margin at 21% (vs. 25% in 2QFY26 and 16% in 1QFY27). Sobha incurred INR6.2b, up 76% YoY, toward land investment during the quarter. We expect a 21% CAGR in residential collections in FY26-28 to INR103b
 Contracts & Manufacturing business reports steady performance 
As of 1HFY27, revenue from the Contracts & Manufacturing business grew 6.8% YoY to INR4.0b, of which INR1.9b (+4.5% YoY) came in from Contracts business and INR2.1b from Manufacturing & Retail. Overall, 1H collections from this division declined by 12.9% YoY to INR3.3b.
* In 2QFY27, revenue declined by 31% YoY to INR9.7b. EBITDA fell 28% YoY to INR687m, with EBITDA margins of 7.1%. Adj. PAT declined 54.6% YoY to INR330m, with PAT margin of 6.1%.
* As of 1HFY27, revenue remained flat YoY at INR22.4b. EBITDA increased 23% YoY to INR1.5b, with EBITDA margins of 6.5%. Adj. PAT declined 3% YoY to INR838m with PAT margin of 3.7%.
* The company reported net cash of INR3.2b as of 2QFY27
* Ongoing and upcoming projects are valued on a DCF basis at INR148b.
* We have factored in land value from only the subsequent projects (191 acres/ 15.6msf) that are in the future pipeline. However, we are now not factoring in any value from the additional 1,745 acres of land, which is still under various stages of consolidation. We would consider value from these land parcels once there are concrete plans in place. Hence, the TP is revised to INR1,710, indicating a 45% upside potential. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock.

docs.title: Buy Oberoi Realty Ltd for the Target Rs.2,145 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
In-line 2Q; new launches to drive FY27E pre-sales In 2QFY27, Oberoi Realty (OBER)’s pre-sales surged 6x YoY to INR91.5b (in line), driven by exceptional bookings of ~INR79b at its maiden NCR project – Three Sixty North (Gurugram). The project contributed 86% of quarterly pre-sales. Three Sixty West (Worli) witnessed a pick-up with ~INR2.8b presales in 2Q (~3% share). Further, the Thane projects witnessed better traction, as total sales (Jardin + Forestville) stood at ~INR2.1b (~2% share). The launch pipeline for 2HFY27 includes Aurelius (Pedder Road), Alibaug, and new towers at Jardin and Forestville, and Adarsh Nagar (contingent on approvals), which would drive presales in the coming quarters. We tweak our estimates for FY27 to INR135b (+149% YoY) to incorporate the net sales in NCR and maintain our estimate for FY28 at INR112b (17% YoY decline due to a high base in FY27).
 Annuity and hospitality portfolio ramping up well 
Rental revenue grew 17% YoY to INR3.4b in 2QFY27. Occupancy was healthy at 96-100% across Commerz I, II, and III, while Oberoi Mall’s occupancy stood at 99%. Sky City Mall occupancy improved marginally to 83% from 82% in 1QFY27. Overall occupancy across annuity assets stood at 95%, with an EBITDA margin of 93% at quarter-end. On the back of healthy occupancy and rental escalations, we retain our annuity income CAGR estimate of 10% to INR13.7b over FY26-28.
Hospitality revenue stood at INR456m in 2QFY27, up 2% YoY, while RevPAR increased 8% YoY to ~INR11,933 and ARR rose 15% YoY to INR15,780. Occupancy remained stable at 75%. The Ritz-Carlton at Three Sixty West and the Marriott hotel in Borivali are expected to commence operations in FY28. We therefore expect a 56% CAGR in hospitality revenue to INR4.8b during FY26-28.
 Balance sheet remains sturdy; NOCF generation healthy 
Collections in 2QFY27 grew 40% YoY to ~INR19b in 2QFY27. During FY26-28, we estimate collections will record a 27% CAGR to INR69b, supported by strong pre-sales and healthy execution. OBER generated net OCF of INR18.1b during the quarter with ~80% NOCF margin. Its net cash-to-equity ratio stood at 0.02x. Supported by strong cash flows from the residential, annuity and hospitality segments, we expect net cash of INR5.3b/INR15.5b in FY27/28E, respectively
* In 2QFY27, revenue dipped 6% YoY to INR16.7b. EBITDA was flat YoY at INR10.2b (in line), while the EBITDA margin expanded 460bp QoQ to 61.0%. PAT remained flat YoY at INR7.6b (in line with estimates).
* In 1HFY27, revenue grew 7% YoY to INR29.7b. EBITDA was up 14% YoY to INR17.5b, while the margin came in at 59%. PAT was up 10% YoY to INR13.1b.
* OBER is likely to report a jump in pre-sales in FY27 given the robust response in NCR and its launch pipeline. Further, the strong ramp-up in business development activity has improved the medium-term growth visibility. The annuity and hospitality segments are scaling up well, and with more additions already planned, we expect profitability to grow strongly in the coming years. In addition, it has one of the strongest balance sheets among peers, which lends comfort.

docs.text:
Strong volume growth; pricing recovery gaining traction Cost pressure to persist in near term; planning next phase of expansion

However, near-term cost pressure persists due to elevated input material costs. The company is evaluating its next phase of organic capacity expansion beyond 240mtpa (by FY28E), with detailed plans to be announced before FY27-end. It is scaling up its C&W business, with a focus on product availability and execution.
* We maintain our earnings estimates for FY27/FY28. We value UTCEM at 18x FY28E EV/EBITDA to arrive at a TP of INR13,220. Reiterate BUY.
 Sales volume up ~13% YoY; blended realization up ~5% YoY to INR6,095

RMC revenue grew ~29% (+17% vs. estimate) and white cement revenue grew ~4% YoY (in line). Other operating income/t stood at INR71 vs. INR70/INR44 in 2QFY26/1QFY27.
* Blended realization rose ~5% YoY/2% QoQ. Grey cement domestic realization increased ~2% YoY (down ~1% QoQ). Opex/t increased ~5% YoY (+8% QoQ), led by ~8%/3%/2% increase in variable/freight cost/other expenses per ton, while staff cost/t declined ~3% YoY. EBITDA/t increased ~7% YoY to INR974. Depreciation/interest costs rose ~6%/20% YoY, while other income declined ~36% YoY. ETR was 27.0% vs. 25.1%/25.2% in 2QFY26/1QFY27.
* In 1HFY27, revenue/EBITDA/PAT grew 17%/16%/18% YoY to INR479.4b/INR87.4b/INR41.1b. OPM contracted 20bp YoY to ~18%. EBITDA/t increased 3% YoY to INR1,099. OCF stood at INR69.1b vs. INR55.7b in 1HFY26. Capex stood at INR57.7b vs. INR48.0b in 1HFY26. FCF stood at INR11.4b vs. INR7.7b in 1HFY26. Net debt stood at INR235b vs INR166b in Mar’26.
* UTCEM’s 2QFY27 performance was in line with our estimates. The company reported robust volume growth and witnessed strong improvement in capacity utilization. Cement prices have recovered since Sep’26 and seen improvement in early-Oct’26. However, cost pressure remains a key near-term challenge. UTCEM continues to extend its lead over peers across capacity, market share, cost leadership, and cash flow generation.
* We estimate a CAGR of 13%/14%/15% in consolidated revenue/EBITDA/PAT over FY26-28. We estimate its consolidated volume CAGR at ~10% and EBITDA/t of INR1,130/INR1,186 in FY27/FY28 vs. INR1,103 in FY26. The net debt-toEBITDA ratio is estimated to remain range-bound between 0.8x and 1.0x. We estimate its RoE/RoCE to increase to ~13%/12% by FY28 from ~11%/10% in FY26, led by an improvement in profitability and lower costs for expansions.
* The stock is currently trading at 17x/14x FY27E/FY28E EV/EBITDA. We value UTCEM at 18x FY28E EV/EBITDA to arrive at a TP of INR13,220. Reiterate BUY.

docs.title: Buy L&T Finance Ltd for the Target Rs 330 by Emkay Global Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
LTF reported another strong quarter, with its highest-ever PAT of Rs9.7bn (+33% yoy) and AUM of Rs1.37trn (+28% yoy), led by robust disbursements in Gold Loans, Personal Loans, and SME. Credit costs declined 8bps qoq to 2.46%, aided by better collections and AI-led tools (Cyclops, Nostradamus). The management remains confident of >20% AUM growth, NIM+fees at 10– 10.5%, and credit costs of ~2–2.2% by FY27 exit. It expects ROA to reach ~2.8–3.0% by FY27 exit and 3.0–3.2% by FY31. While monitoring the West Asia conflict and drought in some pockets, it sees no stress build-up, given limited exposure to affected areas (Rs10.3bn, ~3.3% of rural group loans/MFI book). On the IRDAI draft, the management expects a softer landing via FIDC, with offsets through payments/PPI fees, AI-led opex savings, and Hercules-led cross-sell. Strong growth in Gold Loans, Micro LAP, and Personal Loans, along with Hercules-led cross-sell, should support growth and margins. The recordlow COF of 6.95% provides a cushion against further repo hikes. Factoring in the recent performance and outlook, we adjust our estimates marginally, while maintaining BUY and Sep-27E TP of Rs330, implying an FY28E PBV 2.4x.
 Strong quarter; lower COF drives profitability 
LTF reported a strong quarter, with PAT of Rs9.7bn (+6%/33% qoq/yoy), beating our estimates, mainly due to lower-than-expected COF. AUM grew 5%/28% qoq/yoy, led by healthy retail disbursements (~Rs240bn, +27% yoy). NIM+fees was stable at 10.48%, as ~34bps qoq NIM expansion to 8.88% was offset by lower fee and other income (1.60% vs 1.93%). The NIM gain came from a 25bps qoq fall in COF to a record-low 6.95%. Opex-to-AUM rose slightly to 4.08% on branch and tech investments, while credit cost declined 8bps qoq to 2.46%. Asset quality improved, with GS3/NS3 at 2.75%/0.85%, and ROA/ROE stood at 2.60%/13.56%.
 Lakshya 2031 intact; 2H momentum to strengthen further 
LTF expects business momentum to strengthen in 3Q on festive demand and a calibrated rural pickup, with RBF collection efficiency steady at 99.7–99.8%. It remains confident of its Lakshya 2031 targets, with credit costs expected to fall to ~2–2.2% by 4QFY27 (≤2% over the medium term), supported by Cyclops-led underwriting, a prime-focused book, and CGFMU/CGTMSE cover. Despite further repo hikes, NIM+fees should stay around the middle of the 10–10.5% range, aided by a record-low COF of 6.95%, lockedin funding (for the next 3-4 quarters), and HL repricing. LTF expects a softer landing on insurance fee income and is diversifying into payments/PPI and Hercules-led cross-sell. It plans ~800 gold loan branches by FY27 end and targets gold loan AUM of Rs400– 450bn by FY31 (~14-15% of AUM). In personal loans, it expects the monthly run-rate to rise to Rs17–18bn from Rs14–15bn as Cyclops integration nears completion. Improving credit costs and operating leverage should drive ROA to ~2.8–3.0% by FY27 exit
 Marginally adjust estimates, reiterate BUY 
Reflecting 2Q performance and developments, we marginally adjust our estimates and reiterate BUY with a Sep-27E TP of Rs330, implying 2.4x FY28E PBV. Key monitorables: IRDAI guidelines, rural asset quality, PL ramp-up, and COF trajectory amid repo hikes.

On Monday the stock slipped about 3.4% to Rs 565.65 by 3:23 PM IST, in a market where the Sensex fell about 1.2%. docs.title: Buy DLF Ltd for the Target Rs.780 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
New launches expected to drive presales Beat on presales, driven by new launches 
In 2QFY27, DLF’s presales declined 12% YoY to INR38.0b, but were much higher than our estimates of INR26b, driven by the complete sell-out of the new project — The Aureva, Gurugram (INR19b) — and sustenance sales from The Dahlias (INR18b). In 1HFY27, the company’s sales stood at INR44.6b, down 72% YoY. Over the medium term, DLF has a launch pipeline of ~INR582b, which includes two major launches earmarked for FY27 — Westpark P-2 in Mumbai and Magnolias P-2 (DLF Phase IV). Further, out of the projects already launched, DLF has a balance inventory worth ~INR150b, which is likely to support presales in the upcoming quarters. Based on its launch plans, we expect a 2% presales CAGR, reaching INR209b over FY26-28.
 Occupancy remains high in the annuity portfolio 
DCCDL’s rental income in 2QFY27 increased 9% YoY to INR14.8b, driven by steady growth across the portfolio (DLF + DCCDL + Atrium rentals at INR17.0b). Overall occupancy in the office portfolio stood at a record 96% (99% nonSEZ/91% SEZ), while retail occupancy stood at 97%. DCCDL’s net debt increased by INR2.8b QoQ to INR184b.
DLF's Rentco portfolio is expected to achieve exit rentals of INR7.5b (annualized), excluding Atrium, while DCCDL's exit rentals are expected at ~INR68b. The recent commissioning of Summit Plaza and Midtown Plaza, along with the expected commissioning of Promenade Goa at the end of 3QFY27, should support incremental rental income. We expect rental income of INR71b/INR79b in FY27/28.
 Strong cash generation; balance sheet remains sturdy 
Residential collections inched up 3% YoY to INR26b, in line. DLF generated operating cashflows of INR18.6b. Consequently, despite a dividend outflow of INR19.8b, the decline in net cash was contained at INR150.8b (70% in RERA accounts), which was INR1.2b lower QoQ. DCCDL’s net debt increased by INR2.8b QoQ to INR184b, with a net debt-to-GAV ratio of 0.18x. Cost of debt improved to 7.04% from 7.14% in 1QFY27.
DLF’s 2QFY27 revenue declined 23% YoY to INR12.6b, while EBITDA dipped 92% YoY to INR230m. EBITDA margin was muted at 1.8%, sharply lower than our estimate. Adj. PAT rose 38% YoY to INR13b, driven by a one-time revaluation gain worth INR7.4b on an investment recognized under other income. Excluding this, PAT was much lower than expected. Out of the inventory launched until 2QFY27, the company has a surplus cash potential of ~INR425b. It also has a residual gross margin of INR395b yet to be recognized.
DLF’s 1HFY27 revenue declined 42% YoY to INR25.4b, while EBITDA fell 73% YoY to INR1.7b. EBITDA margin stood at 6.8%. Adj. PAT increased 23% YoY to INR21b.
We value DLF at its NAV and currently do not assign a growth premium to it since the potential of its sizable landbank is already getting captured in our estimates. Further, delta to valuations would come via new project additions in MMR and/or other markets. We therefore believe the company’s valuation at 0% NAV premium is justified. We marginally raise the WACC for the residential portfolio to 11.0% (10.8% earlier) and widen the cap rate to 8.0% (from 7.5%) to value the commercial portfolio. However, since we roll over the valuation to FY28 for residential portfolio, the TP has increased to INR780. We reiterate our BUY rating.

docs.title: Buy HDFC Bank Ltd for the Target Rs 1,050 by Emkay Global Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
HDFC Bank reported PAT of Rs195bn/ROA of 1.8%, broadly in line with our estimates. PPOP grew 5.6% yoy/4.7% qoq, while core PPOP grew 12.4% yoy/3.4% qoq. Loan growth improved further to 16.4% yoy, driven by broadbased growth across segments and a pickup in retail, while growth excluding FCNR(B) leverage remained healthy at 14.4% yoy. Deposit growth was strong at 18.8% yoy/4.9% qoq, supported by FCNR(B) flows. NIM declined by 8bps qoq to 3.3% due to FCNR(B) funding and stable COF; the recent rate hike should provide support, partly offset by the full-quarter impact of FCNR(B), keeping margins broadly stable in 3Q. We believe the appointment of a new MD and CEO should resolve the prolonged succession overhang and help restore customer and investor confidence. Following the stock’s sustained underperformance, valuations have turned attractive, offering scope for a sustained re-rating as the new leadership makes progress on key priorities and geopolitical uncertainties ease, potentially moderating or reversing FPI outflows (refer to our note: Link). We reiterate BUY on HDFCB with unchanged TP of Rs1,050 (2.0x Sep-28E ABV + Rs121/sh for subsidiaries).
 Healthy business growth; margin decline qoq 
HDFCB’s credit growth continued to improve, rising 16.4% yoy/5.2% qoq, driven by the SME and corporate segments. Retail growth also picked up, to 11.7% yoy/6.5% qoq, supported by broad-based growth across products after remaining subdued in previous quarters. Credit growth excluding FCNR(B) leverage remained healthy at 14.4% yoy/3.4% qoq. Deposit growth was strong at 18.8% yoy/4.9% qoq, led by robust TD accretion amid strong FCNR(B) flows, while CASA grew 10.8% yoy/2.6% qoq, resulting in CASA ratio of 31.6%. Retail deposits were stable, at 80% of total deposits. NIM declined by 8bps qoq to 3.32%, reflecting the FCNR(B) impact and stable costs. While the recent rate hike is expected to support margins, the full-quarter impact of FCNR(B) funding is likely to offset part of the benefit, keeping margins broadly stable in 3Q.
Slippages moderated to Rs61bn (0.9% of loans), while better recoveries and write-offs drove a 6bps qoq decline in GNPA to 1.1%. Specific PCR improved to 67%, although it remains below the optimal level of ~70%. The management has not observed any material stress or deterioration in agri asset quality so far, but will continue to monitor the impact of uneven monsoon distribution on crop yields and farm incomes.
We largely retain our earnings estimates and expect ROA to steadily improve (1.8-1.9% over FY27-29E). We maintain BUY with unchanged TP of Rs1,050 (valuing the standalone bank at 2.0x Sep-28E ABV and subsidiaries at Rs121/share). Key risks: Slower-thanexpected growth due to macro weakness and KMP attrition.

docs.title: Buy Axis Bank Ltd for the Target Rs 1,600 by Emkay Global Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Axis Bank reported PAT of ~Rs70bn (up 38% yoy/down 1.6% qoq), 2% below our estimate, while PPOP at Rs110.8bn missed our estimate by 6%. The miss was due to lower other income and elevated operating expenses, partly offset by provisions coming 23% below our estimate. Opex increased 9% yoy/11% qoq to Rs108.2bn, including Rs2.5bn of one-off costs related mainly to labor codes and FCNR(B) mobilization. Despite this, cost-to-assets declined by 6bps qoq/24 bps yoy to 2.14%. Provisions fell 52% yoy, with credit costs declining to 54bps, supported by lower slippages (1.7%) and improving asset quality (GNPA at 1.16%, down by 12bps qoq). Advances grew 23% yoy/9% qoq, supporting the growth outlook, although FCNR(B)-related pressure weighed on NIM. Management expects margin to improve as FCNR(B) funds are deployed and higher-cost deposits are retired. The ECL transition impact is expected to be manageable, supported by ~Rs80bn of contingent provisions. Improving margins, operating efficiency, and credit costs are expected to drive up ROA to 1.4–1.5% over FY27-29E.The stock is currently trading at cheap valuations of 1.3x Sep-28E P/ABV. Hence, we retain BUY on Axis Bank with unchanged TP to Rs1,600, rolling forward Standalone bank valuations on 1.6x Jun-28E P/ABV and subs at Rs137/sh.
 Strong Advances growth; Margin to improve Advances grew 23% yoy/9% qoq, led by corporate (up 34% yoy) and commercial (up 29% yoy) banking. Deposits rose 20.7% yoy/5.8% qoq, driven by term deposits (up 27% yoy/8.4% qoq), while CASA ratio declined to ~32%. The FCNR(B) mobilization contributed ~Rs1,018bn, with ~8% market share. NIM declined by 10bps qoq to 3.36%, reflecting a 11bps drag from FCNR(B) mobilization and deployment, partly offset by lower interest reversals. Ex FCNR(B), NIM was 3.47%, up by 1bp qoq, as liability repricing partly offset the impact of repo-rate cuts and adverse balance-sheet mix. Management expects margin to improve over 3Q–4QFY27 as FCNR(B) funds are deployed into advances and higher-cost non-retail term deposits are retired.
 Asset quality improves; ECL impact manageable Asset quality improved, with gross slippage ratio declining by 31bps qoq to 1.48%, reflecting broad-based improvement across portfolios. GNPA fell by 12bps qoq to 1.16%, while NNPA declined by 4bps to 0.35%. Credit costs fell to 54bps, the lowest in several quarters. Recoveries from written-off accounts rose 51% yoy to Rs9.7bn, reflecting underlying recovery trends rather than one-off gains. Management expects further credit-cost improvement, while the ECL transition impact is expected to be manageable, supported by ~Rs80bn of additional provisions
 We retain BUY with unchanged TP of Rs1,600 Improving margins, operating efficiency, and credit costs are expected to drive ROA to 1.4-1.5% over FY27–29E. Hence, we retain BUY with unchanged TP of Rs1,600, rolling forward the SA bank valuation on 1.6x Sep-28E P/ABV and subs at Rs137/sh. Key risks: macro dislocation, delay in unsecured retail NPA stress moderation and KMP attrition.

docs.title: Buy Angel One Ltd for the Target Rs.380 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Strong operational performance; operating margin at 45%+ 
* Angel One’s (ANGELONE) total income at INR10.9b (up 16% YoY/down 1% QoQ) was 5% above our estimates. For 1HFY27, total income grew 20% YoY. The beat was driven by distribution income, supported by strong credit distribution and robust IPO activity during the quarter.
* Total operating expenses declined 3% YoY/19% QoQ to INR6b (in line). Operating margin was 45.1% in 2QFY27, compared to 34.5% in 2QFY26, with standalone margin at 48.9%.
* The beat in other income and operational efficienciesresulted in a 17% PAT beat, with PAT at INR3.3b, growing 58% YoY/ 45% QoQ. For 1HFY27, PAT grew 74% YoY.
* October options ADTO rose 39% month-to-date, signaling a strong recovery in activity. The recent CAS circular is expected to further support derivative volumes post implementation. Management expects standalone margins of ~45% and consolidated margins of 42–45% in FY27.
* We raise our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates by 6%/4%, considering the strong performance in 2QFY27 as well as normalizing derivative activity following the implementation of CAS modifications. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a revised TP of INR380 (premised on 22x FY28E EPS).
 CAS impacts broking; MTF and distribution surge 
* Gross broking revenue stood at ~INR7.8b in 2QFY27, growing 9% YoY/declining 9% QoQ (in line), leading to a decline in revenue contribution to 55% (60% in 2QFY26). The sequential decline in broking revenue was due to a CAS impact-led slowdown in the F&O segment (F&O brokerage down 14% QoQ; in line). Cash brokerage rose 29% YoY/declined 4% QoQ (in line). Commodity brokerage rose 41% YoY/18% QoQ (18% beat).
* ANGELONE’s order run rate was 5.6m per day in 2QFY27, declining from 6.8m in 1QFY27, driven by a 15% QoQ decline in F&O orders. Cash orders were largely stable sequentially. The commodity segment witnessed a 13% QoQ rise in orders, reaching an all-time high of 45m.
* Average client funding book grew 21% QoQ to INR74.5b. Net interest income grew 27% YoY/7% QoQ to INR3.6b. The exit MTF book for 2QFY27 stood at INR82.1b (INR71.5b in 1QFY27), with 437,000+ clients using the product as of 30 th Sep’26.
* During the quarter, 1.9m unique SIPs were registered, with AUM growing to INR219b (INR206b at the end of 1QFY27). 70% of users have more than 1 SIP.
* Credit disbursal increased 30% QoQ to INR6.9b, with the highest monthly distribution of INR2.8b witnessed in Sep’26. Only 179,000 users of ANGELONE’s 40m user base have availed credit through its platform, highlighting significant opportunity to scale this business.
* Wealth management AUM grew 19% QoQ to INR160b, with ARR contribution at 86%. Active assets stood at INR158.8b. UHNI AUM grew 17.5% QoQ to INR102.6b, while the total client base stood at 2,975+
* Distribution income grew 66% QoQ to INR713m, supported by a strong recovery in credit distribution as well as IPO activity during the quarter.
* Asset management AUM stood at INR5.7b as of Sep’26. The AUM is spread across 11 live schemes, with several folios growing to over 259,000.
* Employee expenses declined 7% YoY/5% QoQ to INR2.6b (in line), driven by attrition and ESOP reversal. Management expects employee expenses for FY27 to be ~INR11b, supported by a slower pace of backfilling. Admin expenses remained flat YoY at INR3.4b (in line).
* A sequentially flattish performance in top-line in 2QFY27 was attributed to a drop in F&O activity, offset by strong distribution income, continuously expanding MTF book, and the highest-ever commodity activity. Other new businesses, such as the distribution of fixed deposits, wealth management, and AMC, are likely to gain traction over the medium term.
* On the cost front, lower employee expenses due to attrition and ESOP reversals resulted in robust operating profits, which were offset slightly by an increase in other expenses due to higher client acquisitions during the quarter. We expect consolidated operating margins to remain in the 42-45% range in FY27, supported by strong standalone operating margin (48.9% in 2QFY27).
* We raise our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates by 6%/4%, considering the strong performance in 2QFY27 as well as normalizing derivative activity following the implementation of CAS modifications. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a revised TP of INR380 (premised on 22x FY28E EPS)

docs.title: Buy Metro Brands Ltd for the Target Rs 1,150 by Emkay Global Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
We maintain BUY on Metro Brands, while cutting our TP by ~8% to Rs1,150 from Rs1,250 (50x Sep-28E EPS vs 54x earlier), on a relatively slower ramp-up of FILA/Foot Locker/Walkway. The TP cut is multiple-led as the cut in topline growth is offset by better margins on slower expansion. 2Q operating performance was 3-4% ahead of estimates, led by better gross margin as topline was in line at ~12% yoy. The 2Q topline growth moderation is a blip, as the festive shift impacted growth by 250-350bps; Metro remains confident of delivering mid-teens topline growth as it expects a relatively stronger 2H, helped by a festive shift. Store expansion was muted, at 21 net additions in 1H vs outlook of triple-digit additions in FY27 (post-1Q). Despite building in a slower ramp-up, we maintain our positive stance on the back of strong midteens growth prospects, bolstered by its existing portfolio (Metro/Mochi/Walkway/Crocs), new scalable partnerships (Foot Locker/ FILA/Clarks), and optionality from a healthy balance sheet (~40% cash at FY26-end). The stock has been an underperformer (CY26TD: -23%), and new growth engines/leadership investments have to fire for the stock to re-rate, in our view.
 Revenue in-line; gross-margin expansion drives EBITDA beat 
Revenue grew ~12% yoy (in line with our/street estimates), though impacted by the festive shift (~250-350bps) to 3Q. Among channels, growth was broad-based at 11-12% for both offline (in-store) and e-com (including omni-channel). 2Q online mix remained flat at 14.2% of topline. Revenue per sqft for in-store sales remained broadly flat at Rs4,250 in 2Q (vs Rs4,300 in 2QFY26). Store additions were relatively muted at 12 net stores in 2Q (21 gross additions). Net store additions moderated to 21 in 1HFY27 vs 58 in 1HFY26, as the company tightened store-opening criteria amid elevated rentals. However, management expects store additions to improve in 2HFY27, while remaining focused on opening profitable stores. Premium formats Crocs/Metro/Mochi saw 5/4/2 additions, respectively, while Walkway expansion slowed with 2 additions. Gross margin expanded by ~210bps yoy to 57.4%, driven by lower discounting during end-of-season sales along with a slight improvement in mark-ups. EBITDA margin expansion was limited to ~80bps at 27% due to higher employee expenses (up by ~140bps) due to minimum wage hikes and team investments. EBITDA at Rs1.9bn grew ~16% yoy and was ~4% higher than our estimate. Reported PAT came in at ~Rs758mn, up ~12% yoy though margin at 10.4% was flat yoy due to higher depreciation and lower treasury income.
 Clarks EBO launch expected in 2H; refining Walkway’s expansion strategy 
Clarks’ women’s range is now available across 400+ MBOs, while a limited men’s range is available across 100+ MBOs. The complete store-exclusive range is expected to become available in 3Q and on its D2C website, with Clarks EBOs planned for 2HFY27, subject to supply and assortment stabilization. Walkway’s existing-store initiatives continue to perform well, while the company refines its new-store expansion strategy amid mixed performance from recently opened stores.

docs.title: Buy Urban Company Ltd for the Target Rs 200 by Emkay Global Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Urban Company (UC) delivered a healthy 2QFY27 performance, with the India Consumer Services (ex Instahelp) (ICS) NTV growing 26.3% yoy on a higher base, while International NTV increased 66.9% yoy. InstaHelp orders grew 63.0% qoq to 6.23mn. The Board granted in-principle approval for exploring residential air conditioners under Native and a fund-raise of up to Rs25bn to support organic growth, strengthen InstaHelp’s market leadership, and pursue selective acquisitions. With cash and equivalents of Rs19bn sufficient to fund InstaHelp, the management positioned the proposed raise to provide strategic flexibility while retaining its profitability targets. We revise our NTV (ex KSA) estimates up by 3-5% to incorporate the NTV beat. Each of UC’s segments has a long growth runway, given strong local network, a monopoly core business, and higher margin relative to other internet businesses. We maintain BUY while revising up our TP by ~5.3% to Rs200.
 Core and International margins improve; InstaHelp investments remain elevated 
ICS NTV grew 26.3% yoy to Rs9.63bn, led by 37.0% NTV growth in Tier 2 cities. Revenue rose 28.0% to Rs3.36bn, with ATUs up 22.4% and spend-per-user up 3.2%. Adj EBITDA grew 85.0% yoy to Rs340mn, with margin expanding by 110bps to 3.5% of NTV; the management remains focused on growth, while progressing toward its 9-10% steady-state adj EBITDAM target. InstaHelp orders rose 63% qoq (43% in 1Q) to 6.23mn, while adj EBITDA loss per order reduced to Rs279 from Rs346, while absolute adj EBITDA loss increase to Rs1.74bn amid expansion; investments remain elevated, with breakeven targeted for FY31. International NTV grew 66.2% yoy to Rs2.67bn, with margin expanding by 190bps to 2.0%. The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) JV’s NTV grew 153% yoy to Rs930mn, with adj EBITDA margin improving to -17.3% from -55.3% and breakeven expected over the next few quarters.
 Product expansion in Native; Rs25bn fund raise adds flexibility 
Native NTV grew 35.4% yoy to Rs1.32bn, with revenue of Rs1.05bn and adj EBITDA of Rs(90.0)mn. The management guides for 50–55% yoy 2Q+3Q NTV growth and breakeven over the next few quarters. The Board granted in-principle approval for exploring residential ACs under Native. While expansion in the AC segment will entail initial cash burn, UC has, in the water purifier segment, demonstrated it can deliver differentiated product offerings and gain market share at profitable unit economics. The proposed fund raise of up to Rs25.0bn would support core and Native growth, InstaHelp leadership, and selective acquisitions.
 Outlook and valuation – Core healthy; InstaHelp execution key 
Low core penetration, Tier 2 expansion, improving International profitability, and approaching KSA breakeven support the outlook. Native offers further growth opportunities, while InstaHelp drives higher engagement. Pricing recovery and unit economics remain key monitorables. The management retained consol adj EBITDA breakeven guidance for 3QFY28 and the Rs10.0bn FY31 target. The fund raise strengthens investment capacity, although deployment and dilution remain valuation considerations. We maintain BUY while raising TP by >5% to Rs200, valuing ICS at Rs110/sh, implying 38.6x FY29E EV/EBITDA, and InstaHelp/International/Native/KSA businesses contributing Rs28/Rs27/Rs17/Rs5/sh to our TP, with net cash of Rs12/sh.

docs.title: Buy HDFC Bank Ltd for the Target Rs.925 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
In-line quarter; NIM declines 10bp QoQ Asset quality remains robust 
* HDFC Bank (HDFCB) reported 2QFY27 profit at INR195.1b (5% YoY/2% QoQ, in line).
* NII grew 10% YoY/3% QoQ to INR346.2b, while NIMs on total assets declined by 10bp QoQ to 3.16% (est. 3.18%) due to an adverse impact of leverage on FCNR(B) deposits.
* Other income declined 4% YoY/rose 8% QoQ to INR138.3b (6% beat), supported by healthy growth in fee income and treasury gains of INR8b.
* Advances book grew by a healthy 16.4% YoY/5.2% QoQ to INR31.96t. Deposits grew 18.8% YoY/4.9% QoQ to INR33.27t, aided by FCNR(B) deposit mobilization of INR1.10t. CD ratio thus increased to 96.0%.
* Fresh slippages declined to INR61b. GNPA/NNPA ratios declined to 1.11%/0.37%. PCR rose to 66.9% (up 138bp QoQ).
* We raise FY27/FY28 earnings estimates by 3.5% each and estimate HDFCB to deliver FY28E RoA/RoE of 1.74%/14.1%. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR925 (1.8x FY28E ABV + INR124 for subs).
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* NIM trajectory will move upward from the next quarter onward. In 3QFY27, the bank shall benefit partly from the rate hike, though it will be offset by fullquarter impact of FCNR(B) deposits.
* The bank disbursed INR410b under the ECLGS 5.0 scheme, the highest among all banks.
* There would be a mix change in employee composition in the long term. More people in frontline and lesser people in backend and some may be moved to tech.
* Growth has been balanced across PL, wheels, gold, agri and MSME
 Valuation and view: Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR925 
HDFCB reported a largely in-line quarter, supported by healthy business growth and strong operating profits, although provisions were elevated. NIMs on total assets contracted by 10bp QoQ to 3.16%, while the bank has guided for NIMs to be on an upward trajectory from hereon. Healthy loan growth was driven by SME segment, while retail loan growth gathered some momentum. Deposit growth was healthy, with FCNR(B) mobilization resulting in the CD ratio inching up to 96.0%. We expect the CD ratio to gradually moderate to ~93% by FY28E through calibrated balance sheet management. The bank maintains contingency and floating provisions of INR156b and INR214b, respectively. Improvement in NIMs from retirement of highcost borrowings and operating leverage should support a gradual improvement in profitability and return ratios in the coming years. We raise FY27/FY28 earnings estimates by 3.5% each and estimate HDFCB to deliver FY28E RoA/RoE of 1.74%/14.1%. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR925 (1.8x FY28E ABV + INR124 for subs).

docs.title: Buy LTM Ltd for the Target Rs.5,050 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Growth moderates; margins capped FY27 growth and margins to track FY26 levels 
* LTM reported revenue of USD1.2b in 2QFY27, rising 1.1% QoQ in constant currency (CC) vs. our estimate of 0.9% QoQ CC. EBIT margin at 15.6% was largely in line with our estimate of 15.7%. Adj. PAT came in at INR14b, declining 6.0% QoQ but remaining flat YoY and below our estimate of INR15b.
* In INR terms, revenue/EBIT/adj. PAT grew 15.7%/19.1%/8.1% YoY in 1HFY27. In 2HFY27, we expect revenue/EBIT/adj. PAT to grow 9.7%/10.6%/10.9% YoY. We reiterate BUY with a TP of INR5,050 (valuing at 21x FY28E EPS), implying ~15% upside
 Our view: Consolidated margin expansion to remain muted 
* Revenue growth was relatively soft in 2QFY27, with the Middle East impact expected to weigh on FY27 performance. We do not expect growth acceleration in FY27 and maintain our 5.1% YoY CC growth estimate, as the Middle East business weighed on 2QFY27 QoQ CC growth by ~60–70bp. Excluding this, growth would have been ~1.7–1.8% QoQ CC. However, we believe that the outlook for FY28 remains positive.
* Limited margin expansion: In 1QFY27, management expected continued organic margin expansion, with consolidated margins at FY26 levels or higher. However, in 2QFY27, it adopted a more cautious stance, guiding for FY27 margins to remain closer to the FY26 level of 15.4%, including Randstad, citing acquisition-related amortisation. Traditional-services pricing pressure and an unfavorable revenue mix could further constrain expansion. We lower our FY27 EBIT margin estimate by ~20bp to 15.6%.
* AI-led deals are shorter-tenured and offer faster revenue conversion: TCV stood at USD1.3b, with a significant proportion comprising ACV rather than traditional multi-year TCV. AI-led engagements involve faster revenue realization, given shorter transition periods and quicker deployment. AI revenue increased 40% YoY to 13.4% of revenue in 2QFY27, compared with ~12% in 1QFY27. The gross margin profile of AI projects is higher than that of traditional services. The CBDT engagement contributed to 2QFY27 revenue, with a gradual ramp-up expected as hardware availability has improved.
* Randstad integration remains on track: Approvals for the acquisition of Randstad’s digital businesses in Europe and Australia are expected by the end of 3QFY27, followed by closure and integration. The acquired capabilities are expected to support expansion into newer markets.
* Cash conversion was affected by timing-related outflows: OCF to PAT declined to 39% in 2QFY27 from 79% in 1QFY27, primarily due to gratuity funding against provisions recognized in 3QFY26, advance-tax payments in India and the US, and TDS on the final dividend paid in 1QFY27. Most gratuity funding has been completed, although some outflow may continue in 3QFY27; cash conversion is expected to normalize progressively.
* We believe LTM’s FY26-28 USD revenue CAGR of ~6% remains ahead of most large-caps peers, despite the Middle East impact. We expect growth and margins to improve in FY28 as deal TCV pivots toward short-term AI deals, which convert into revenue faster and offer higher margins.
* We maintain our EPS estimates for FY28, while lowering FY27 EPS estimates mainly due to continued foreign exchange losses for the next two quarters, which will lead to slight under-delivery of earnings. We value LTM at 21x FY28E EPS (20x earlier) due to better growth and margin outlook for FY28, resulting in a revised TP of INR5,050, implying ~15% upside. We reiterate BUY.

docs.title: Buy Federal Bank Ltd for the Target Rs.385 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Steady quarter; treasury gains drive earnings beat NIM stable at 3.32%; core fee income gaining momentum 
* Federal Bank (FB) reported 2QFY27 PAT of INR13.9b (up 45% YoY/18% QoQ, 10% beat), led by higher other income and lower-than-expected provisions. This was partly offset by higher opex, including a one-time impact of INR0.33b due to a change in ESOP accounting.
* NII grew 26% YoY/7% QoQ to INR31.5b (in line). NIM contracted 1bp QoQ to 3.32% (vs MOFSLe of 3.18%).
* Advances grew 22% YoY/7.5% QoQ to INR2.98t, led by the SME, gold, and corporate segments. Deposits grew 18.6% YoY/7.1% QoQ to INR3.42t, aided by FNCR(B) mobilization of INR149b. Leverage provided against FCNR(B) deposits was INR94b. The CASA mix declined 19bp QoQ to 32.0%.
* Provisions declined 6% YoY/rose 8% QoQ to INR3.4b. Slippages rose 3% QoQ to INR4.26b. GNPA/NNPA ratios improved 20bp/1bp QoQ to 1.32%/0.17%. PCR declined 59bp QoQ to ~86.8%.
* We tweak our PAT estimates for FY27/FY28, factoring in higher other income, partly offset by higher opex. We estimate FB to deliver FY27E RoA/RoE of 1.30%/12.4%. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR385 (based on 1.9x FY28E ABV).
 Strong business growth; asset quality healthy 
* FB reported 2Q earnings of INR13.9b (up 45% YoY/down 18% QoQ, 10% beat) amid higher other income and lower provisions, partially offset by higher opex.
* NII grew 26% YoY/7% QoQ to INR31.5b (in line). NIM contracted 1bp QoQ to 3.32% (vs MOFSLe of 3.18%), as a 4bp QoQ reduction in CoF was largely offset by a 3bp QoQ decline in YoA.
* Other income rose 38% YoY/42% QoQ to INR14.9b (27% beat) amid strong treasury income of INR2380m, supported by the encashment of SR investments and robust IPOs.
* Opex grew 21% YoY/15% QoQ (in line), with a one-time adverse impact of INR0.33b from the change in ESOP accounting. C/I ratio stood at 52.1%. The bank expects opex ratios to remain sticky in the near term. PPoP increased 35% YoY/17% QoQ to INR22.3b (8% beat).
* Advances grew by a healthy 22% YoY/7.5% QoQ to INR2.98t, driven by robust growth in SME (19.9% YoY/7.2% QoQ), gold (37% YoY/ 6.7% QoQ), and corporate (14% YoY/4% QoQ). Retail book grew 19.9% YoY (7.2% QoQ), with leverage provided against FCNR(B) deposits of INR94b. PL and CC grew by a healthy 6% and 7% QoQ, respectively.
* Deposits grew 18.6% YoY/7.1% QoQ to INR3.42t, aided by FCNR(B) deposits of INR149b. CASA deposits grew 6.4% QoQ, with the CASA mix declining 19bp QoQ to 32.0%.
* Provisions declined 6% YoY/rose 8% QoQ to INR3.4b. Slippages rose 3% QoQ to INR4.26b (INR4.12b in 1QFY27). GNPA/NNPA ratios improved 20bp/1bp QoQ to 1.32%/ 0.17%.
 Valuation and view: Reiterate BUY with TP of INR385 
FB reported an in-line quarter, supported by strong other income and lower provisions, partly offset by higher opex. NIMs were stable at 3.32% (-1bp QoQ), with reduction in CoF being offset by a decline in yield on advances. Loan growth remained healthy, led by the SME, gold loan, and corporate segments. The bank has guided for loan growth in the mid-teens range, led by medium- to high-yielding segments. Deposit growth stood at 19% YoY, driven by healthy FCNR(B) deposit mobilization. CASA deposits grew 6% QoQ, led by strong traction in current accounts. Asset quality improved, with both GNPA and NNPA ratios declining further. We estimate credit cost to remain contained at ~45-50bp over FY27-28. We tweak our PAT estimates for FY27/FY28, factoring in higher other income, partly offset by higher opex. We estimate FB to deliver FY27E RoA/RoE of 1.30%/12.4%. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR385 (based on 1.9x FY28E ABV)

* Metro Brands (MBL)’s revenue growth further moderated to ~12% YoY in 2Q (from ~15%/20% YoY in 1QFY27/4QFY26) due to a shift in festive dates.
* However, reported EBITDA surged ~16% YoY, as ~215bp YoY gross margin expansion offsets the drag from higher minimum wages.
* MBL’s 1HFY27 revenue and reported EBITDA grew ~13% YoY. However, operating deleverage from higher rentals and lower treasury income lead to a muted ~8% and 2% YoY growth in pre-IND AS EBITDA and PAT, respectively.
* MBL management continues to guide for 15-18% revenue growth over the medium term. However, muted store openings in 1HFY27, a conservative approach to store openings, and BIS-related challenges persisting in the S&A portfolio (Foot Locker, FILA, and MetroActiv) could create short term bumps in the growth rates, in our view.
* We cut our FY27-29E pre-IND AS EBITDA/PAT by 3-6% and model a 13%/12%/11% CAGR in revenue/pre-IND AS EBITDA/PAT over FY26-29E.
 * We reiterate our BUY rating with a revised TP of INR1,075, premised on ~35x Dec’28 pre-IND AS EV/EBITDA (implying ~53x Dec’28 EPS).
 Higher rentals weigh on pre-IND AS EBITDA and profitability in 1HFY27 
* MBL’s 1HFY27 consol. revenue/EBITDA/PAT grew ~13%/13%/2% YoY, as higher D&A (+17% YoY) and lower other income (-13% YoY) weighed on profitability.
* Its 1H Pre-Ind AS EBITDA grew 8% YoY to INR2.45b, as margin dipped ~85bp YoY to 16.9%, due to higher rentals (+21% YoY) from new format additions.
* Net working capital days increased to ~94 days (vs. 82 days in 1HFY26), driven by an increase in inventory days to 115 (from 109 YoY) and lower payable days (36 vs. 44 YoY). Absolute Core WC stood at INR7.8b (up 33% YoY).
* MBL’s 1H pre-IND AS OCF improved to INR812m (vs. INR31m in 1HFY26), largely driven by a lower working capital build-up (INR1.1b vs. INR1.8b YoY). Further, with capex moderating ~8% YoY, 1H pre-IND AS FCF improved to INR248m (vs. an FCF outflow of INR580m YoY).

docs.title: Buy Punjab National Bank Ltd for the Target Rs.140 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Margin expands 8bp QoQ; lower LLP drives earnings beat 
 Asset quality improves – ECL transition requirement lowered 
* Punjab National Bank (PNB) reported 2QFY27 PAT of INR55.3b (up 13% YoY/5% QoQ, a 7% beat on MOFSLe), driven by lower provisions and other income.
* NII grew 11% YoY (up 7% QoQ) to INR116b (4% beat), led by a global NIM expansion of 8bp QoQ to 2.58%.
* Loan book grew 16% YoY (6% QoQ), while deposits grew 10% YoY (3% QoQ). CD ratio increased to 74% from 72% in 1QFY27. ? Slippages increased to INR23.4b from INR20.8b in 1QFY27 due to a slippage in the corporate segment (road account). GNPA/NNPA ratios declined 23bp/3bp QoQ to 2.55%/0.25%. PCR ratio remained stable at 90.3%.
* We tweak our earnings estimates by +1%/+1.4% for FY27/FY28, and estimate FY27E RoA/RoE of 1.05%/15.5%. Reiterate BUY with a revised TP of INR140 (premised on 1x FY28E ABV).
 NIM to expand ~7-9bp sequentially; RoA guided at >1% 
* PNB reported a PAT of INR55.3b (up 13% YoY/5% QoQ, 7% beat) amid lower provisions.
* NII grew 10.8% YoY/7.4% QoQ as global NIM expanded 8bp QoQ to 2.58%. The NIM expansion was led by a decline in cost of deposits (down 3bp QoQ to 4.96%), driven by the retirement of high cost liabilities using FCNR (b) mobilization, while yield on advances improved 7bp QoQ to 7.6%, with a focus on moving to higher yielding assets.
* Other income declined 17% YoY to INR36b amid lower treasury and fee income.
* Opex rose 1.1% YoY/0.8% QoQ to INR76.7b (in line with MOFSLe) amid lower employee costs of INR44b. C/I ratio, thus, declined 75bp YoY/rose 15bp QoQ to 50.5%.
* PPoP largely stood flat QoQ (up 4.2% YoY, largely in line). Provisions declined 82% QoQ, led by a write-back of INR7.9b on one standard account, while additional standard provisions of INR1.25b were made to support the ECL transition.
* The bank revised its one-time ECL transition impact to ~INR80b, while targeting a sustained RoA of 1% and a steady-state credit cost of ~0.25% to 0.3%.
* The loan book grew 16% YoY (6% QoQ) to INR13.1t amid broad-based growth in corporate (3.8% QoQ), agri (5.9% QoQ), and MSME loans (5.7% QoQ). Retail (incl. IBPC) grew 16.3% YoY/5.6% QoQ.
* Deposits grew 10% YoY/3% QoQ to INR17.7t. CASA ratio declined to 36.6% (down 14bp QoQ). The CD ratio, thus, increased to 73.7%.
* On the asset quality front, slippages increased 15.1% QoQ to INR23.95b due to a slippage in a corporate segment – road account. GNPA/ NNPA ratios, thus, declined 23bp/3bp QoQ to 2.55%/0.25%, while PCR ratio was stable at 90.3%.
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* Management revised its estimated one-time ECL transition requirement to ~INR80b from INR90–100b previously, with the residual requirement indicated at INR43–50b.
* The incremental steady-state credit-cost impact from ECL was indicated at ~15bp, with overall credit costs expected at 25–30bp.
* Around 56% of the loan book is repo-linked and reprices the following day. The bank expects 25bp repo rate hike to support NIM by 7–9bp and yield on advances by ~10bp in the coming quarter.
* SMA-0 stood at INR169.6b/1.26%, SMA-1 at INR74.6b/0.56%, and SMA-2 at INR89.8b/0.67%.
* Average gold loan yield stood at 8.6%, with management expecting an increase to 8.75–8.90%. Agri gold loan book stood at 94% of the total gold loan portfolio
 Valuation and view: Reiterate BUY with a revised TP of INR140 
PNB reported a strong quarter, with earnings beat led by controlled provisions and opex, while margins expanded 8bp QoQ. Provisions came in lower, reflecting strong asset quality, even as they created additional standard asset provisions to facilitate a smoother transition to ECL. The bank lowered its one-time ECL impact guidance to ~INR80b. Asset quality trends remained healthy, with marginal uptick in slippages driven by a single infrastructure corporate account and no significant stress elsewhere in the portfolio. Management guided for RoA of >1% and credit cost of 0.25–0.30% We estimate FY27E RoA/RoE of 1.05%/15.5% and reiterate our BUY rating with a revised TP of INR140 (premised on 1x FY28E ABV).
